hypothesis.claim: One single-flight scheduler per adapter, adapter-level coalescing and runner decimation remove the F18 clash without slowing the live view or adding scans
hypothesis.disconfirming_result: Concurrent requests issue more than one scan, a test sharing the live cadence records the wrong number of cycles, or real-adapter cycles fail/stale when live + test run together

decision.why: DR-0011: one owner of scanning; consumers reuse each scan; a mutex would serialise and double the scan rate

change.summary: IScanScheduler/ScanScheduler (cadence = min request, single flight, AutoScan flag), WlanAdapter in-flight coalescing, SaturationTestRunner on the scheduler with decimation (tolerance = half effective interval), shared scheduler in DI
change.scope_authority: Owner approval 2026-10-16 (E-0008, Q5 'fix F18 first'); DR-0011

negative: Loop stops when cadences are released
Mutant without single flight is killed

what_worked: Mutation check proves the regression test
Hardware probe from the test project
what_failed: First design ran the first scan asynchronously in headless VMs (would race tests) -> AutoScan flag

reuse.reuse_applied: Fresh-scan cycle semantics from IT-T03 unchanged

lessons.transferable_rule: Give a shared hardware resource exactly one owner loop; consumers subscribe and decimate

next_action.action: Owner trial with live view + capture + test together on real networks
